title: First Rate
body:
Everything about using this app has been pleasing to me.

The app interface is simple and intuitive, whilst also providing all the functions that spring to mind.  During my initial subscription month, which expired on the day I wrote this review, I emailed the developer a feature related question. He responded within hours. Twice. Outstanding support. As such, I am buying the app outright.

I think this app is well suited to the subscription model, as learning new habits might occur over only a few months. That said, I am not generally a fan of subscription models and prefer to buy. In this case the developer also seems to have put some careful thought toward the pricing structure, as it seems reasonable to me at each price point (monthly or annual subscription, or buy).

Finally, and also importantly, the app does not needlessly collect data. This is a significant positive given the fact that many others apps track you. 

So, if you want to change your habits, and are looking for a reasonably priced and simple to use app - this may be for you!

title: Great app, a few bugs, a couple problems
body:
I love how simplified the designers have made this app. They don't try to attract you with bells and whistles, Just a responsive User Interface with a decent amount of  customization. 

Bugs: 
- I have the premium version, but sometimes when the app treats me as if I am on the free version, not allowing me to view stats. Closing and reopening the app doesn't work, and neither does tapping 'restore purchases'
- The app allows you to pause and track timers out of the notification center, which is a feature I love, but sometimes the display time is not synced up with the app's actual time. for example lets say I started a timer for habit A, do A for 15 minutes, pause the out-of-app timer and then close my phone; 30 minutes later the out-of-app display will show 45 minutes as if i never paused it, but the in-app timer will always have the correct data. Since the correct data is stored, it's not a huge issue but still can be confusing when it looks like i left the timer on for the whole day.

Problems
- The biggest problem is that while you can add infinite habits, I have about 40 that i track and it can feel a bit cluttered with anything past 20. Adding a new habit can be annoying because if i want to change the order of the habits I have to drag it up past 20 others and that can get annoying trying to drag up a whole group of habits. 
- The other issue with a lot of habits is that it feels inefficient to scroll past a bunch of habits, I feel like this could be fixed by allowing to filter habits through color, or by which list they belong to.

title: Awesome app that can be improved further
body:
I love how reliable, useful, and usable the app is. I also very much appreciate its integration with Apple Health and its seamless synchronization across my devices.  Special kudos to the UX! If I were to suggest further improvements to make it even more awesome, these would as follows:
Ability to choose between distance and time for such endurance workouts as running, hiking, walking, swimming, cycling, etc.
Ability to combine several endurance workouts (such as those listed above). I want just to reach a weekly goal of doing so many hours of endurance workouts every week, rather than have seepage goals for cycling, swimming, running, hiking, etc.
Ability to set a goal for so many minutes per week of Zone 2 training (not sure if Apple Health API allows collection of such data).
Ability to assign different weights (e.g., between 1 and 10) to different habits, depending on their importance/priority for me. This way, the percentage achieved every day/week/month would be a function of those weights.
Overall a great app for gamifying habit development and tracking one’s habits. Big thanks to the developer(s)!

title: The best habit tracker available
body: I've tried many trackers in the past. This one is by far the best for my use case and I have been using it almost continuously for the past 2 years. Some people may be motivated by more bells and whistles, like planting virtual trees and watching them grow, but those things are not for me. I like the clean aesthetic and thoughtful approach and functionality of this app, and the excellent and completely seamless interaction across all my devices. In addition, the product is reasonably priced. I especially like the one-time purchase option in this age of inevitable subscription models. With simplicity comes results - by setting small goals and following through, I have finally rediscovered my ability to focus and read over the past two years, finishing dozens of books I would not have otherwise. It offers good integration with Apple Health (I try to hit 10.000 steps a day and stay below a certain calorie intake), includes timers (I am using it to track my 16/8 fasting as well as 90 mins deep work sessions) but also the simple build a habit (flossing teeth) or break a habit (no screens late evening). title: Impeccable !

- très réactive : non seulement les données se mettent à jour sur tous les appareils rapidement mais l’app elle-même répond à toutes entrées immédiatement. Pas besoin d’appuyer 3 fois sur un bouton pour que ça réponde (et ce n’est pas le cas d’autres app de ce type).

- On ne peut pas moduler les valeurs d’objectifs suivant le jour : par exemple je souhaite faire 1h de vélo certains jours et seulement 15 ou 30 min d’autres jours. En l’état je contourne le problème en créant un deuxième objectif identique mais avec une valeur différente. Mais le développeur pourrait peut-être ajouter cette possibilité à l’avenir.

Au vu de toutes les qualités de l’app, après quelques semaines sur la version gratuite j’ai craqué pour la version payante à vie (25€ au moment ou j’écris. Je ne souscris jamais d’abonnement pour un logiciel). L’achat débloque toutes les fonctions en particulier la personnalisation avec des icônes et des couleurs et un nombre illimité d’objectifs.
Très satisfait. Bravo au développeur.

title: "Better, Not Perfect"
body:
The focus on percentages to measure accomplishment in a day is THE crucial thing that makes this app great, because as someone who suffers from perfectionism and binary thinking it means that accomplishment becomes far more nuanced and relative - you're never thinking about the cliff edge of losing a streak or success/failure binary that then makes you feel like a failure,  discourages you from even trying and turns your behavior into fatalist protection from anxiety.

The flexibility of a percentage instead reinforces the idea of doing your best, it allows you to say, "hey I got 80% of the things i wanted to build habits for, that's pretty good for my circumstances today!", or "i have about 60% right now, is there something i could do to push that number a little higher?".  I get to treat my habit goals as a natural cluster of things to tend to beside my current life rather than a terrifyingly rigid law that slices through it, and i can still zoom in to still see the new habit ideas i'm not doing or having trouble with and figure out how to make that work.

There's other great features like the simple native UI, the full Apple Watch and Widgets integration and the option for a one time purchase, but the percentage focus and backseating of streaks made this a thing i actually use and bought over the hundreds of habit apps i browsed and dozen or so I attempted using.

My critiques are minor and mainly relate to laggy or non-existant background updates for complications on my Watch, the fact longer habit names get cut off in the UI, and the grouping system.  For groups id like to be able to see them more easily at a glance and define them in the Atomic Habits sense of "this is their purpose, this is what i'm trying to become through them", but the current filter system obscures and fences that sense of purpose off more than id like.

title: Not sure why there needs to be a subscription
body:

Usually when apps charge a subscription they can often justify it by saying that your data is stored in your account for that service, which obviously takes up storage for the developer and server bandwidth and whatnot. However this app just uses iCloud to sync, which I already pay for. I don’t understand why I would also need to subscribe when all the operations of the app would be taking place on my device or through iCloud which I’m paying for, not the developer. 

The developer might say that they need to charge a subscription to fund development, but that only flys as a reason if the user expects frequent development and new features. Habit trackers don’t tend to need constant new features - there is a certain point at which an app becomes a good habit tracker. Development can be funded to this point through one time purchases. 

Hard to see the subscription model here as anything other than a cash grab.

Before my journey into habit development, I was using time trackers, as I found it useful to see where my time was going. However I started to get anxious by seeing my time lost in activities I didn’t care about, and got no motivation to achieve what I wanted during the day in the first place, as there is no real place to set goals… and that’s where Awesome Habits came in. 
Habits still allows me to time track an activity, but now not just any activity. It’s specific activities I care about and just those. 

The customer support is great too. I asked if it was possible to integrate Awesome Habits with other time tracking apps, via Zapier or IFTTT, or have access to to export/import functionality, and their was reply was really positive!

I’m looking forward to future developments. Thank you for making the app!

title: reliable, beautiful, well designed (a joy to use), affordable
body:
I have gone through a dozen habit tracking and time tracking apps, and purchased several also. 

This is the only app I've found which :

1.  treats time management at the same level as habits (eg ATracker buries goals in a separate page)

2. allows for timer & integer habits (incl 0 : yes some apps don't allow 0 as input lol, a necessity for tracking bad habit "unstreaks")

3. allows you to specify if a habit is good or bad (incl distinctly visualising that aspect)

4. doesn't limit the number of tracked habits (Streaks has a limit of 12 due to their design).

If you don't want to have to open multiple apps to track timer & goal based habits, then this is the best designed in that space. It is also more beautiful & fun to use than any other app I have come across in either field, which means it will get used daily :-).

App & touch performance is pro-level, and what users have come to expect, although some in this space don't tick either of those basics!

The non-subscription price of this app is in the middle of the range of prices for these apps. Which makes it affordable to all (thank you).

I give it a 5/5 score because it covers all my core requirements extremely well. As with all things, there can always be improvements, lol, so here is my wishlist for less important functionality (that could attract more users to it) :

1. tags to filter a long list of habits (the app does allow for distinctly coloured icons which almost achieves the same thing though)

2. tracking of start & end times, and allowing multiple segments in a timer-based habit (it could show the total, and then drill into the habit to show a list of segments : this would encroach on the time management apps' field!)

3. adding an overall note to a habit (it could simply be a single line of font size 8) to allow users to make a note of what they did wrong last time that broken their habit streak

4. there is some Apple HealthKit data which I don't use atm, but it could go even further (eg sleep hours, weight, etc)

5. there is one minor crash which can occur on editing the list for reordering habits (it rarely occurs, because I rarely need to reorder habits, and is therefore avoidable ... but the app instantly reloads with the same state anyway)

6. it's not mentioned in many comparative app review websites or youtube channels

Finally, my thanks go out to the clearly highly intelligent designer/developer for producing such a nice app, and giving us a non-subscription option.

title: Eddig a legmegbízhatóbb
body:
Még az ingyenes Awesome Habits alkalmazást használtam, mikor a készítőtől sokat kérdeztem, aki mindenre válaszolt. Nem sokkal ezután kifejtettem, a tapasztalatom alapján, hogy az alkalmazása a legjobb, amely elérhető. Erre megkért, hogy írjam le ezt az AppStore-ban is. Azt mondtam, ezt majd megteszem akkor, ha eltelik pár hónap és látom, az alkalmazás hosszútávon hogyan működik.

Két hónap telt el azóta. Így már látom, a napi szintű használat mellett, hogy milyen az Awesome Habits.

A közel fél éven át tartó kutatásaim és teszteléseim során a piacon elérhető összes szokáskezelőt és projektkezelőt kipróbáltam. Ezek között volt a monday.com, a Clickup, a Trello és még sok más. Már a nevükre sem emlékszem. Az OmniGroup szoftverekre még igen, azokra még emlékszem. Jók voltak, már amennyiben mindenből kikerült a cég által használt adatbázis, mert ennek kezelése az OmniGroup által borzalmasan rossz volt és akkor is az volt, míg az előfizetőjük voltam.

Egy újabb befutóval találkoztam és ezt is kitanultam, azaz gyakoroltam. Elolvastam mindent, amit csak lehetett, megnéztem minden oktatóanyagot és minden funkciót újra és újra begyakorolva a látottak, az olvasottak szerint, hogy lássam, hogyan működik az alkalmazás.

Mint említettem, az összes nagy és kevésbé neves projektkezelőt kitanultam egy bizonyos szinten használni sok-sok gyakorlással. Ideértve az összes nagy és kevésbé híres szokáskezelőket is.

Mindegyik projekt- és szokáskezelő megbízhatatlan, rossz, azaz hibás, tehát nem működik. Nem véletlen, hogy azóta sem használom egyik projektkezelőt sem. És a prognózis szerint, nem is fogom használni egyiket sem a közeljövőben, pont az említett funkciók stagnáló megbízhatatlansági rátája miatt.

Az egyik tesztalanyom az Awesome Habits volt, aminek a véleményét írom éppen. A két hónap használt után mint előfizető, leírom, hogy milyen.

Ez az egyedüli alkalmazás, ahol az export közel 100%-os. A többi szokáskezelőnél vagy nincsen vagy rossz, avagy használhatatlan formátumú, így még az 1%-ot sem érik el.

Az Awesome Habits stabil, megbízható. Sosem hibázik, nem fagy ki és van szupport, aki támogat.

Hozzáteszem, semmiféle anyagi haszon vagy bármiféle előnyöm nem származott és nem is fog abból, hogy leírtam, milyen az Awesome Habits, aminek a véleményeit olvassa éppen. Ezek az én személyes tapasztalataim a két hónapnyi, napi szintű intenzív használat után.

Ajánlom ezt az alkalmazást, mert a használatom óta kiadott verziói 100%-ban megbízhatóak jelenleg, stabilan működnek iPhone-on, jó az éves díjazása, van szupport és érti is a kérdéseket, amelyeket elfogadható időn belül érthetően megválaszol.

body:

I have used many Habit tracking apps but without any hesitation I can say, it is the best habit tracking app available on App Store. The app has got everything that a user would need. With cloud backup, it works on all three devices : iPhone, Mac, watch.

User should be able to get a photo of monthly/yearly recap, which contains maybe heat maps, or some other stats clearly depicting the progress made at the end of a month and at the end of year. User can share that picture on social media. It’s a Win Win situation for both parties. User will get more motivation from this, and it will help developer to promote the app.

I usually do not write such long reviews, but the app is so awesome that I had to write one. Kudos to developer for all the effort in creating and maintaining such a beautiful app. I just hope we get to see the above 3 feature request in near future.

title: The only habit tracker that actually changed my behavior
body:
I’ve tried many habit trackers over the years, but Awesome Habits is the first one that genuinely became part of my life.

What I love most is how simple and frictionless it feels. There is no unnecessary complexity, no gamification overload, no feeling that managing the habit tracker becomes a habit in itself. You open the app, see exactly what matters, complete your habits, and move on with your day.

Over time, that simplicity had a much bigger effect on me than I expected. Awesome Habits helped me turn things I wanted to do occasionally into things I now do consistently. Health, supplementation, training, routines and other small daily behaviors became much easier to maintain because I could actually see my consistency accumulating over months.

The statistics are also extremely motivating. Seeing long streaks, completion history and hundreds of completed repetitions creates a real sense of continuity. You stop thinking about habits as isolated actions and start seeing them as part of your identity and long-term system.

The design deserves a mention too. It is clean, beautiful and incredibly pleasant to use. It feels like an app designed by people who understand that the best productivity software should reduce friction rather than create more of it.

I recently sent the team a small product suggestion and was genuinely surprised to receive a thoughtful personal response from the developer, who actually understood the idea and added it to their list for future updates. That level of care is rare.

Awesome Habits may look like a simple habit tracker, but for me it has had a surprisingly meaningful impact on how I organize my life and maintain consistency.

One of the very few apps on my phone that I would immediately reinstall on a new device.

There were others that worked well but mixed up the data. And some were bearable, but had a JSON export that wasn’t very useful. 

I was about to give up my long search when I came across the Awesome Habits software. 

I started testing it, and the developer was constantly helping me because I had plenty of questions. Once I saw that this app was good, I purchased it. And it’s been perfect ever since, especially the CSV export.

title: Timestamp option for habit completions
body:
Thank you for creating such a great habit app! I’m currently using the free trial, and a couple of my buddies and I are considering the one-time purchase.

One feature we’d really love to see is the ability to add or edit a timestamp for each habit completion. This would make the history much more accurate, especially when we forget to mark a habit right away.

This would be a very useful feature and would make the app even more valuable for us. Thanks again!

title: Awesome Habits. Awesome App.
body:
Every time I start with a new productivity system I over complicate it. Not with this. Empty rings bad. Filled rings good. Habits are incredibly simple to set up and customize. Back filling is easy and day/week/month views are great. The widgets put habits front and center and performing a habit has become a welcome alternative to getting swept up in social media. 

With my setup, a “meh” day means about 70%— C work, but a better baseline (and better streaks!) than I’ve had in the past. 100% days really count and include a mix of baseline habits, tracked dietary needs, and other positive activities. 

I only have two (minor) complaints:
- You can seemingly only change the primary ring color by changing the app to mono. Can we please set the primary ring color separately?
- Similarly, you can’t set colors on lists, so you have to manage lists and colors separately. List colors, still separate from individual habit colors but with the option to apply to all habits, would be hugely appreciated. 

Wishlist:
- Expanding on the above, a view with a circle for each list’s progress with respective colors + an icon for each
- Mark a habit as “Bonus” so it contributes to the total percentage in a way that can exceed 100%

My recommendation— Get it. There are similar apps out there, but none that balance simplicity and functionality in such a satisfyingly iOS-like way.

title: Intuitive, and powerful
body:
When I first loaded this app, it was almost easy to mistake it for any other habit tracker because of it doesn’t try to overcomplicate the user with too many features. But if you dig deeper, the amount of customization and power sets this app apart from the others. 

Pros: 
 - Clean simple design. 
- Lots of customization of your habit list. 
- Fast cross device syncing. 
- Widgets have lots of options and sizes. 
- Can show the live habit timer inside a widget. 
- Live activities for habit timers. 
- Apps for every Apple device including MacOS. 
- Add urls or Apple Shortcuts to habits to quick launch whatever you want. 
- Apple Shortcut actions with almost full control over everything in the app. 

As an example power feature, you can use quick launch on a habit to launch an Apple Shortcut which marks the habit as complete, and then launches whatever else you want, creating a perfect automation companion for your habits. 

Cons: 
- The app needs to open for every Apple Shortcut action you launch. I really hope the developer can make this work in the background so Apple Shortcut Personal Automations will work with my phone locked. 
- More widget options couldn’t hurt, like having one for a “up next” habit which shows the next goal in your habit list for the day. 

As you can see, the cons are extremely minor, this app deserves five stars even despite those. Highly recommend this app if you are looking for a simple yet powerful habit app.

title: Great UI and UX!
body:
A lot of thought went into this app and it shows. So easy to use and a pleasant experience to mark goals complete. Tap the widget, tap the goal, and done. Or use Siri Shortcuts. This is perfect.

I was wondering if you have a roadmap anywhere on what improvements might be coming down the pipe. Some apps have an entire week view with little colored or uncolered squares showing if a goal was completed. It’s a cool way to pack a lot of data, like 10 goals over a week, and view it all at once.

Another cool feature would be multi level goals to track workouts, like the habit could be bench press, the # of reps would another dimension, and the weight would be the 3rd level dimension. Getting data in for weight and reps would mean you completed the goal of bench press, but would be cool to track weight and reps in a way that could be displayed on graphs. So not just using the notes feature for this.

Lastly, for the hardcore nerds among us, csv export of all the data in case we want to juxtapose our goals alongside data from other apps that we are tracking. Like overlaying our goals data on a graph from our smart scale app that shows our weight/ muscle mass/etc. exporting the data makes this possible and allows for the potential to make some amazing insights on how our habits can correlate to other things that we are tracking.

This app should become the solution to track everything else. We have Apple Watch and smart scales to track so many things, overlaying that data on top of anything else we want to track should make this a must have app.

title: A fairly viable Streaks alternative
body:
Some things it shares with Streaks:

- Just recently, it added the ability to attach a URL to a habit.

Here’s what it has over Streaks right now:

- Unlimited habits. You aren’t limited to 24.

- Habit categorization: via lists, which operate like tags, meaning you can add multiple lists to one habit

- The ability to add units past a goal

  - With Streaks, once you get the habit done, that’s it. You can’t, say, add one more hour to a Play Piano habit because you already hit your goal.

  - Awesome let’s you add more hours even when you hit your goal, making it more close to Strides in tracking.

- Just recently, it added the ability to attach a description to a habit.

Here’s where it lacks:

- It’s library of Apple Health synced habits is still limited when compared to Streaks. I don’t believe I can sync things like tooth brushing.

- You can only run one timer at once and it must be done while the app is still open. If you exit the screen, the timer will stop.

- Lack of badges. You’ll have to enter the app each time to know how many habits you have yet to complete.

- The only way to filter habits is via lists. You can’t text search them or filter them by status yet.

title: Very nice so far, with a couple suggestions
body:
I haven't been using the app for very long yet, but after trying a number of habit tracking apps trying to find one that works for me I am enjoying this one. Pleasing interface, simple yet varied habit type setup, easy to use and nice apple watch app and widgets. There are a couple of things I'm missing that other apps had though:
1. The ability to set a habit for "every x days," such as for something I want to do every 3 days as opposed to on specific days of the week. I unexpectedly found this very helpful on other apps so I'm missing it now.
2. Snoozing habits. There's a skip button but if you're traveling it could be a pain to have to skip habits every day that you can't do while away from home. Maybe archiving & then un-archiving could do this? I haven't had a need to try it yet.
3. This one isn't something I expect to change, but I do wish more habit apps had a visual monthly overview of what days you completed what habits. I'm a visual person when it comes to tracking time and also have a hard time remembering when I did or didn't do things. I'd find some kind of overall calendar view much more useful than a line graph, but I know not everyone is the same. There is a streaks chart of sorts for this using lines for individual habits so that's better than nothing.
4. I meant to stop at 3 but I just remembered: can there be a way to not include habit breaking apps in the daily status ring? I have a simple 'eat fewer sweets' habit set to 3 sweets max but it means i always start my day with the ring partially completed, which feels counterintuitive. I'd rather just not include habit breaking habits in the status ring at all, or have them hurt it somehow if you go over instead of making it look like you already did something at the start of the day.

title: Perfect in every way
body: I’ve never reviewed an app before, but I had to come here to gush about how amazing this app is. I’ve tried so, so many habit trackers... some paid, some free, some that took me hours to set up. I’ve been using apps for habit tracking for about 3 years, and probably tried at least 20 apps, and there’s always something not quite right. So this morning I downloaded this app and THIS IS IT. There is just so much to like, but I will try to summarize: the option to have completed tasks move automatically to the bottom of the list, so you can glance at the top to see what to do next (why is this not always a thing?!) ...how it groups tasks by frequency (daily, weekly, monthly) so you can see clearly what you have to do today, but *still see your other tasks too* (this alone makes Awesome Habits better than all the competition, because you don’t have to assign a specific day of the week to see your weekly/monthly tasks in the standard view). The actually functional status ring that lets me choose whether I want to track only today’s tasks or all of them — so having weekly tasks doesn’t have to mean you’re never “done” with everything.  AND, if that wasn’t enough, it is not only iPhone, iPad, Watch (and Mac!) compatible, but the different apps are all thoughtfully done and the syncing is GREAT. It has Watch complications that show the status ring  % complete for the day, and it actually syncs, and fast, between your devices. The iPhone app even has widgets that I actually want to use! It’s beautiful to look at, customizable but still simple, does everything I want and things I didn’t even know I wanted, but has no extra bulk or fluff. And finally — you choose to pay a reasonable one-time fee instead of a subscription. This app is good enough that I would maybe even consider a subscription, but the option to pay once makes this a no-brainer to me. If I could give more stars I would. Totally life changing. Thank you so much for creating this.
